name: John Wayne Sweep
description: The John Wayne Sweep is a half-guard knee-lever reversal that anchors the opponent's lower leg and tips the hips while the bottom player controls the upper-body posts.
summary: The John Wayne Sweep is a half-guard knee-lever reversal that anchors the opponent's lower leg and tips the hips while the bottom player controls the upper-body posts.
overview:
The bottom player has half guard around one leg, with a usable underhook/whizzer relationship and a lower-leg anchor. Shawn Williams demonstrates a shallow foot anchor and knee lever, finishing on top in half guard. A butterfly-hook position and direct mount are not the demonstrated start and finish.

Contain one opposing leg while keeping your own knee free to act as a lever. Use an underhook and control the whizzer or posting arm without leaving the elbow exposed to a front-headlock attack. Place a shallow foot connection over the ankle or shin rather than locking the knee into a deep hook.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Shawn Williams — John Wayne sweep from half guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dKlm6xRmpIA).

attacker.name: John Wayne Sweep Attacker
attacker.description: John Wayne Sweep (attacker): Contain one opposing leg while keeping your own knee free to act as a lever. Use an underhook and control the whizzer or posting arm without leaving the elbow exposed to a front-headlock attack.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player has half guard around one leg, with a usable underhook/whizzer relationship and a lower-leg anchor. Shawn Williams demonstrates a shallow foot anchor and knee lever, finishing on top in half guard. A butterfly-hook position and direct mount are not the demonstrated start and finish.

Contain one opposing leg while keeping your own knee free to act as a lever. Use an underhook and control the whizzer or posting arm without leaving the elbow exposed to a front-headlock attack. Place a shallow foot connection over the ankle or shin rather than locking the knee into a deep hook.

Bring the knee into the hip line as the other foot supplies a controlled post. Rotate the hips and upper body so the leg anchor and controlled post cooperate. Establish top half guard before attempting to free the remaining leg or advance to mount.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Keep the underhooking elbow outside your hip to deny the Darce choke, and use the free hand to prevent a crossface while setting the knee lever. After coming on top, near-side underhook and shoulder pressure help free the head and begin passing the remaining half guard; this continuation follows the reversal rather than replacing it.

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): What must your half-guard leg connection leave available?
flashcards.answer: Contain one opposing leg while keeping your own knee free to act as a lever.
flashcards.answer_line: A knee free to act on the opponent's hip

plausible: A knee buried beneath the opponent's trapped thigh
A free foot while your knee remains clamped underneath
trap: A knee held against your own chest below their hip line

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): Against a whizzer, where should the underhooking elbow stay?
flashcards.answer: Williams keeps the underhooking elbow outside the hip to preserve leverage and reduce Darce exposure.

plausible: Folded inward across your belly
Behind your hip with the arm stretched

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): Where does the shallow lower-leg anchor sit?
flashcards.answer: Place a shallow foot connection over the ankle or shin rather than locking the knee into a deep hook.
flashcards.answer_line: The foot just over the opponent's ankle or shin

plausible: Deep behind the knee with your knee buried
High around the upper thigh with your knee tucked beneath
trap: Beyond the toes with no ankle or shin contact

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): Where does the levering knee act?
flashcards.answer: Bring the knee into the hip line as the other foot supplies a controlled post.

plausible: Below the hip against the lower thigh
Across the upper ribs above the waist
trap: Into the lower shin near the ankle

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): What coordinates the reversal?
flashcards.answer: Rotate the hips and upper body so the leg anchor and controlled post cooperate.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee lever and leg anchor with upper-body post control

plausible: A straight-arm bench press without moving the hips
A kick upward while releasing the anchored leg
trap: A knee lift while allowing the near hand to post

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): Where does Williams settle immediately after the sweep?
flashcards.answer: Establish top half guard before attempting to free the remaining leg or advance to mount.

plausible: Directly in mount with both legs clear
On top in side control, legs free

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): What guard supplies the demonstrated starting position?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player has half guard around one leg, with a usable underhook/whizzer relationship and a lower-leg anchor.
flashcards.answer_line: Half guard with an underhook and shallow leg anchor

plausible: Deep half with the lower leg shelved on your shoulder
Butterfly guard with both insteps beneath the thighs
trap: Half guard with the levering knee buried in a deep hook

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): Why avoid a deep lower-leg hook in this version?
flashcards.answer: A shallow ankle/shin connection leaves the knee free to rise into the opponent's hip.
flashcards.answer_line: It can trap your knee and remove the hip lever

plausible: The deeper lower-leg entanglement frees the knee to lead the bridge
The sweep depends on fixing the knee below the opposing ankle
trap: The lower-leg hook replaces the hip contact used to tilt the pelvis

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): The knee becomes fixed during the turn. What should change?
flashcards.answer: Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
flashcards.answer_line: Stop the forced turn and release the leg restraint

plausible: Rotate the torso farther while holding the foot
Continue raising the hip before changing the trapped hook
trap: Pull the anchored foot free while the knee stays fixed

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (bottom): What follows stabilization in top half guard?
flashcards.answer: The near-side underhook and shoulder connection can support a later pass, but the reversal itself ends in half guard.
flashcards.answer_line: A separate attempt to clear the remaining leg

plausible: Counting mount before either leg is released
Release the upper-body connection before freeing the leg
trap: Assuming chest pressure alone removes the hook

defender.description: John Wayne Sweep (defender): A shallow lower-leg anchor with the opposing knee entering your hip signals the sweep. Keep a hand or foot able to support the tipping direction before the upper body is captured.
defender.overview:
The bottom player has half guard around one leg, with a usable underhook/whizzer relationship and a lower-leg anchor. Shawn Williams demonstrates a shallow foot anchor and knee lever, finishing on top in half guard. A butterfly-hook position and direct mount are not the demonstrated start and finish.

A shallow lower-leg anchor with the opposing knee entering your hip signals the sweep. Keep a hand or foot able to support the tipping direction before the upper body is captured. Avoid letting the bottom player connect their upper body directly under your base.

Address the shallow foot anchor while the knee and hip can still move safely. Do not post a locked arm or twist a trapped knee to resist a completed reversal. Use inside frames and the remaining leg connection after the opponent comes on top.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

If the knee lever removes your base, release unsafe arm tension and begin an escape from the position you actually land in. Recover a shoulder frame and inside knee before the new top player closes the space beside your ribs.

Follow the fall safely: Do not post a locked arm or twist a trapped knee to resist a completed reversal.

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (top): Which lower-body pairing signals the knee lever?
flashcards.answer: A shallow lower-leg anchor with the opposing knee entering your hip signals the sweep.
flashcards.answer_line: A shallow ankle anchor with their knee entering your hip

plausible: A deep hook with their levering knee buried below your thigh
A shallow ankle hook with their knee pointing away from your hip
trap: A knee against your hip with your lower leg completely free

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (top): What support matters before the sweep controls your posts?
flashcards.answer: Keep a hand or foot able to support the tipping direction before the upper body is captured.
flashcards.answer_line: A usable hand or foot in the tipping direction

plausible: Both hands reaching across the opponent's far shoulder
The trapped ankle as your only support point
trap: A hand posted on the side opposite the tipping line

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (top): What upper-body connection should you deny early?
flashcards.answer: Avoid letting the bottom player connect their upper body directly under your base.
flashcards.answer_line: Their underhook connecting the torso beneath your base

plausible: Their palm checking your biceps with no underhook beneath you
Their forearm framing your shoulder while the torso stays distant
trap: Their wrist gripping your ankle with the shoulder outside your hip

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (top): When is removing the ankle anchor most appropriate?
flashcards.answer: Address the shallow foot anchor while the knee and hip can still move safely.
flashcards.answer_line: Before the knee and hip are fixed under the lever

plausible: Once the knee is wedged but before your shoulders reach the mat
After the hip begins rotating against the anchored foot
trap: Only after the opponent lands and settles on top

flashcards.question: John Wayne Sweep (top): Your base is already lost. How should you follow the reversal?
flashcards.answer: Do not post a locked arm or twist a trapped knee to resist a completed reversal.
flashcards.answer_line: Accept the fall and rebuild frames from the landing

plausible: Keep the old top posture while reaching behind for a post
Hold the anchored ankle still while your torso continues turning
trap: Turn the trapped knee outward to remain chest-down
